clue.text: Engine makes an American mad, with a reason for action.

parts.note: loco is American slang for crazy or mad
a motive is what moves someone to act

explanation.surface: A Yankee goes crazy, and has his reasons for doing so.
explanation.definitionFit: A locomotive is the powered railway vehicle that pulls a train, so it is an engine.

clue.text: Compose during an interval of calm

definitions.meaning: to compose someone is to soothe or quieten them
a quiet pause in a storm or in activity

explanation.surface: Someone writes music during a quiet spell.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone is to calm them, and a pause in a storm is a quiet spell; one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Risks fortunes?

definitions.meaning: luck, the way things fall out by chance

explanation.definitionFit: A gamble is a hazard you take, and luck or fate is what happens by accident; the same plural covers both.

clue.text: On the trail of a vehicle that overturned on the monarch!

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down entry the word for the vehicle reads upwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: Following a carriage that tipped over on top of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that overturned' turns CART into TRAC; in a down clue 'on' puts it above KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Following someone's trail is pursuing them by their marks, a hunter's sense.

clue.text: Part of the helmet reflected in a corrosive substance?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the run of letters is read in reverse
the letters sit inside the single word corrosive

explanation.surface: A piece of armour seen mirrored in some acid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks ROSIV from inside 'corrosive', and 'reflected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable front of a helmet that shields the face is the visor.

clue.text: Fail to perform in the room itself.

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the words room itself, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Not doing a job in the very room.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a duty undone is to neglect or skip it.

clue.text: Pit-worker takes a novice to see what's dug out of the ground.

definitions.text: what's dug out of the ground

parts.note: a miner works in a coal pit
L, the learner plate, stands for a novice

explanation.surface: A coal miner brings along a beginner to look at what has been excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ores and other inorganic substances extracted by mining are this kind of substance.

clue.text: He's divinely wise — but mightn't he have other hopes?

indicators.note: the question suggests the letters could equally be rearranged to make the other phrase

explanation.surface: A mystic wise man wonders whether his hopes lie elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mightn't he have' suggests the letters of OTHER HOPES rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A theosopher claims mystical insight into the nature of God, divine wisdom.

clue.text: To get things repaired quickly, say this!.

definitions.text: To get things repaired quickly, say this

parts.words: To get things repaired quickly, say this
parts.note: plays on the proverb that the less is said, the sooner a quarrel is mended

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that saying little mends matters soonest, so the word for the smallest amount fits.

clue.text: Warrant issued when.&case runs strangely.

indicators.note: acting strangely implies the letters fall into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A warrant goes out when a court case takes an odd turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee or pledge is a warrant, the sense of a firm promise.

clue.text: Without leaving any part, botanically speaking.

definitions.text: Without leaving any part, botanically speaking.

parts.words: Without leaving any part, botanically speaking
parts.note: a plant pulled up entirely loses its underground and overground parts alike, a picture of total thoroughness

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely and thoroughly, from a plant destroyed down to its base and out to its limbs.

clue.text: Where men move around-especially "one who rebukes groups of directors.

parts.note: to check someone is to rebuke or restrain them
boards are company directors meeting as a body

explanation.surface: An office scene: a scold who dresses down whole boards of directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'men' are the pieces in a board game such as draughts, moved around the squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts pieces are called men, and they are moved about on this squared playing surface.

clue.text: Fee at price arranged for theatrical sketch.

indicators.note: something arranged is set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fee is fixed at a price for a short stage turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic play staged after the main drama was this kind of piece.

clue.text: Ornaments made of stones?

indicators.note: made of suggests something put together, so the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Decorations fashioned out of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlands of flowers or ribbon hung in loops serve as decorations.

clue.text: Ideal spot, for puss to have a rest and a pretty poor drink?

definitions.text: Ideal spot, for puss to have a rest
definitions.meaning: the knees of a seated person, where a pet cat likes to curl up
a weak, watery beverage fit only for a cat

explanation.surface: Where a cat naps, and a feeble beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A seated person's knees are a cat's favourite resting place, and weak tea was mocked as fit only for felines to slurp.

clue.text: More wordy 'publisher.

definitions.meaning: comparative of an adjective meaning verbose or long-winded
one who spreads something abroad, as news is spread

explanation.definitionFit: Diffuse writing is verbose, so this is its comparative; and one who scatters news widely spreads it like a publisher.

clue.text: Leaving out and dropping one element of part of the play.

indicators.note: one letter, an element of the word, is dropped from the passage

parts.note: an excerpt is a passage taken from a play

explanation.surface: Cutting a scene from a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping one element of' removes the R from EXCERPT.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means not including, other than, as in all bar one.

clue.text: Dress offered at a price initially unacceptable to me.

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word only

explanation.surface: A frock on sale at a price I find unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn for a role or period is a dress or outfit.

clue.text: I. bled-bad disablement-but easily managed

indicators.note: a disabled form is damaged, so these letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone bled badly from an injury but proved docile.
explanation.definitionFit: A docile, obedient person is easily controlled.

clue.text: See, I beg wildly and importune.

indicators.note: behaving wildly means the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A beggar pleads frantically with passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset someone with requests is to importune them, a figurative siege.

clue.text: Encounter one definition of a sleeve.

definitions.meaning: a fight or clash between opponents
a sleeve is literally a channel through which a limb goes

explanation.surface: A fight, and what a sleeve really is.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout of combat between knights was so called, and literally a sleeve is the way through for a limb.

clue.text: Measure a little girl, with this result:

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width
Sue is a girl's name, short for Susan

explanation.surface: Measuring a small girl, with this outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence is to result.

parts.words: Allow not nature more than nature- Man's life is cheap as "beast's" (King Lear).
parts.note: Lear's lines with a word missing after the second nature: what nature requires

clue.text: A garden part of it is cultivated enthusiastically.

indicators.note: part of means a run of letters taken from inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A garden that is tended with great zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden of Genesis where Adam and Eve lived is the archetypal garden.

clue.text: Don't probe so much! It's impenetrable!

definitions.meaning: a plea to investigate to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: Stop prying, it cannot be fathomed anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word is an order to investigate less; whole, it means inscrutable, beyond all looking.
